More storage - 64GB now  Now a blue colorway  OneUI8 comes preloaded, and the old ones are getting OneUI8 anyway. So with these software updates and all the changes since the original launched last year, how good is this watch?  I’ll dig into a speaker and mic test, a tour of the UI, heart rate accuracy analysis as well as gps, sleep tracking, and more.  This should be a complete review of the Galaxy Watch Ultra for anyone considering buying one  Durability   Sleep tracking  It tries to give useful insights and I really appreciate that. I know what I am looking for in my numbers, but many people might not. The insights and summaries are nice.    That said, they have been consistently wrong for me. “Did you have stimulants before bed” - no, but I did eat a late dinner.  “Manage your stress levels” - no, it was a really fun and relaxing night.   The sleep stages seem to be relatively accurate. Always some discrepancy between awake time and light sleep, but I do not care about that. Deep sleep and REM are usually pretty close to what my WHOOP, Garmin, and Apple watch devices say  HRV is not very close though - disagrees with many other devices.    I usually average 60 - 70 with some nights hitting the low 100s if I am doing sprint workouts. Galaxy Watch 8 Ultra consistently gives me an AVERAGE of 105ms - I wish that was correct! Hey, maybe everything else is wrong, but I am skeptical of the Galaxy Watch here.  Energy score - Pretty useless. Essentially just a more complex sleep score. I want this to adapt throughout the day like Garmin body battery   Always tells me to prioritize rest. I could get great sleep and have an energy score of 89 and it will tell me to prioritize rest  Battery  I keep AOD on.    I went from 60% yesterday morning to 25% this morning. I throw it on the charger while I shower, brush my teeth, get dressed, etc. That brings me back to 50% so with this method, I’m losing about 10% per day which means I need to do a full recharge about once every 9 days. Not bad!  If I am traveling, it lasts 2.5 - 3 days depending on GPS usage. That means it can barely eek through a weekend and you may want to turn off AOD and use power saving mode  I miss the two week battery life of my Garmin though.     Gemini  Took some adjustment to start using it, but actually sooooo useful    I ask it questions all the time, especially if I am driving and don’t want to use my phone.   It can do things on your watch like start workouts, timers, etc.   It does not answer questions about sleep tracking for example, but instead brings you to the sleep UI  SPEAKER TEST  MICROPHONE TEST  BUTTONS & DESIGN  I actually don’t hate the design. I used to but I sort of like it now   Three buttons is nice, but I made the middle one a double press because I kept accidentally hitting it   I still accidentally press it when I am driving for some reason   Not enough shortcuts for that button - only like 6 options. Not press and hold or single vs double press   Needs something that rotates, a bezel or crown. The digital bezel ain’t it. I only use the “digital bezel” to dismiss timers and phone calls. Otherwise, finger is in the way when spinning   Display is awesome - very easy to read, very bright, very colorful. The redshift is nice in the evening as well

title: Samsung Galaxy Watch Ultra Review | Ultra-Fine?
description: Reviewing the Samsung Galaxy Watch Ultra, a more rugged and premium smartwatch alternative to the Watch 7. This £599 wearable boasts a tough enough design for all of your outdoor fitness shenanigans. The Samsung Galaxy Watch Ultra can tolerate extreme temperatures and take a solid knock, with its Mil STD-810 passing grades.  Yes, that strap and square-ish frame might give this smartwatch Apple-esque vibes, but it's a WearOS device with Samsung's own features slapped on. You've got Play Store access to download fresh apps to the Galaxy Watch Ultra. Plus of course plenty of built-in fitness tracking features. Oh, and Bixby. Can't forget Bixby. No matter how many pints of whisky I smash.  The Samsung Galaxy Watch Ultra has okay-ish battery life, but the 60-ish hours I get from a full charge isn't as good as some rivals. Wear OS rivals like the OnePlus Watch 2 are superior in that department.  Performance is respectable however and the Samsung Galaxy Watch Ultra's super-bright screen is ideal for outdoor use. Add in the water resistance and rugged design, plus emergency features, and the Watch Ultra is good for a weekend away. Doing crazy stuff like cycling through canyons. Personally, I prefer a pint and pork.  So that's my review of the Samsung Galaxy Watch Ultra, let me know your thoughts below!
